A panel of judges today dismissed the Department of Justice's bid
to stop California from processing 20,000 registered voters ballots
in the upcoming midterm election,
as NPR's Jude Joffe-Blanc reports the next step in the case
is a hearing before a federal district judge tomorrow.
The DOJ says some 20,000 people on California's voter rolls
are likely non-citizens, though has not provided detailed evidence.
California officials say the DOJ's list is unreliable
and it's unlawful and infeasible to set aside the ballots
this close to election day.
In a two-to-one decision, a Ninth Circuit panel
dismissed the DOJ's appeal Monday,
finding the case was not ready for appeal
since the district court judge has not yet ruled.
The two judges also made clear they disagreed with DOJ's demands.
Now the case goes back to the district court,
where a hearing is scheduled for Tuesday.
Jude Joffe-Blanc, NPR News.
Montana's competitive first congressional district
is drawing prominent Republican figures
as election day draws closer.
Montana Public Radio's Clayton Murphy
reports on Vice President J.D. Vance's visit
to a district that could help determine control of the House.
In the past two weeks, President Trump, House Speaker Mike Johnson,
and Vice President Vance have stumped in Montana.
The message has been simple. Get out and vote.
Vance's rally in an airport hangar was no different.
Let's send a message to the patriots of Montana
that in this state, we believe in sovereignty.
In this state, we believe in freedom.
Vance stumped for House candidate
and former conservative talk radio host Aaron Flint.
His race against Democrat Sam Forstag,
a former Forest Service smokejumper,
is by most accounts a toss-up.
About a quarter of the state's registered voters
have already voted by mail.
Vance's next stop is Michigan,
where several races are also considered toss-ups.
For NPR News, I'm Clayton Murphy.
And Belgrade, Montana.
The U.S. government is warning that Iran
is trying to target U.S. troops and officials
in the Middle East and elsewhere.
Meanwhile, President Trump and Israeli officials
are both publicly threatening a new round of attacks on Iran.
Former National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan
explains who's being potentially targeted
and how serious the threat is.
This is a familiar pattern with the Iranians
that they would seek to target Americans.
And that could include, Scott,
everything from troops on the front lines,
obviously, who they have been trying to strike
at bases in the Middle East,
up to and including the most senior officials
of the U.S. government.
This is a pattern in practice for the Iranian regime
and something that we do have to take seriously.
Delegations from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan,
and Turkey held talks in Tehran today
to try and prevent more fighting.
U.S. stocks climbed today.
The S&P 500 rose seven-tenths of a percent.
Later this week, earnings reports will come out
from roughly one out of every three stocks
within the S&P 500.
This is NPR News from Washington.
President Trump is suggesting without evidence
that incumbent Brazilian President Ignacio Lula
de Silva's election win yesterday was rigged
after he fended off a challenge from Flavio Bolsonaro.
Bolsonaro has rejected the results.
He's the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro,
who's in prison for planning a coup
following his election loss in 2022.
Heavy rains in the Southwest gave a big boost
to Colorado River flows in the Grand Canyon.
As Alex Hager of member station KJZZ reports,
it's a welcome change in a historically dry year.
Wildlife and sandy beaches inside the Grand Canyon
depend on big rushes of water every once in a while.
But drought and climate change mean lately
there isn't much to send downstream from Lake Powell.
Jen Pels with the nonprofit Grand Canyon Trust says
recent rains caused the highest flows
in at least a couple years.
Having the opportunity to have those high flows
in the canyon is really important from an ecological sense.
It will provide benefits.
River watchers originally thought the flows
may have been even higher than they were.
Deadly flash floods earlier this summer
dammed up a section of the river,
causing the past week's rains to pool
around a remote measuring station
and give misleading data.
For NPR News, I'm Alex Hager in Phoenix.
The NBA has struck deals with prediction markets,
calci and poly market.
The agreements include limitations on offerings,
transparency and suspicious patterns
and bans on league personnel trading on events.
The moves come after the NBA restricted
certain types of betting this season.
And tonight is the sports equinox.
Five pro-American leagues are playing at the same time.
Baseball's World Series,
Monday Night Football, the NBA, WNBA and NHL all have games.
It's NPR.
